Frankly, it’s in line with what dictators in other countries do. This political retribution is a dangerous sign of authoritarianism and cannot be taken lightly. Trump and his administration have made it clear through their nonstop barrage of unconstitutional executive actions that they aren’t just coming for some of us, but all of us. This is an attack on our electoral system, on political dissent, and on you. Together, we can and must fight back. I’ve already filed 14 lawsuits against this administration for other illegal actions that would harm Californians and people across the country, and I’m following this situation very closely. In solidarity, Rob

Fellow activist,

Trump is a step closer to openly defying the courts and deporting people without due process. This is a scary time in America.

In case you missed it, due to an “administrative error,” the Trump regime has deported Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia to a dangerous and violent mega-prison in El Salvador. According to the _New York Times_ , Garcia is a 29-year-old father of three, living in Maryland with protected legal status.

**Here’s what’s happening:** The U.S. Supreme Court has unanimously determined that the government must “facilitate” his return to the United States. However, Trump is indicating that he has no intention of following this order. Instead, he has allied himself with President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador, who self-describes himself as the world’s “coolest dictator,” and has stated, _**“Of course I’m not going to do it,”**_ when asked if he will return Garcia home.

**As Stephen Vladeck, a law professor at Georgetown University, stated to the NYT, “the idea that ‘the government can disappear people to a foreign country with no due process and no responsibility for what happens next’” amounts to “a rule-of-law crisis.”**

If Trump gets away with sending someone, _regardless of their citizenship status_ , to a foreign prison without recourse, the impact could be devastating. This is made abundantly clear as **he has floated the idea of sending American citizens “convicted of violent crimes” to the prison in El Salvador** , and his Attorney General, Pam Bondi, is allegedly studying the proposal.

As the Trump regime works to chip away at our democracy and push us closer to a constitutional crisis, it has never been more critical that our state and federal courts remain fair and independent. The independence of the judiciary should be protected – especially from the executive branch.

clean_body: | | | Fellow activist, Trump is a step closer to openly defying the courts and deporting people without due process. This is a scary time in America. In case you missed it, due to an “administrative error,” the Trump regime has deported Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia to a dangerous and violent mega-prison in El Salvador. According to the New York Times , Garcia is a 29-year-old father of three, living in Maryland with protected legal status. Here’s what’s happening: The U.S. Supreme Court has unanimously determined that the government must “facilitate” his return to the United States. However, Trump is indicating that he has no intention of following this order. Instead, he has allied himself with President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador, who self-describes himself as the world’s “coolest dictator,” and has stated, “Of course I’m not going to do it,” when asked if he will return Garcia home. As Stephen Vladeck, a law professor at Georgetown University, stated to the NYT, “the idea that ‘the government can disappear people to a foreign country with no due process and no responsibility for what happens next’” amounts to “a rule-of-law crisis.” If Trump gets away with sending someone, regardless of their citizenship status , to a foreign prison without recourse, the impact could be devastating. This is made abundantly clear as he has floated the idea of sending American citizens “convicted of violent crimes” to the prison in El Salvador , and his Attorney General, Pam Bondi, is allegedly studying the proposal. As the Trump regime works to chip away at our democracy and push us closer to a constitutional crisis, it has never been more critical that our state and federal courts remain fair and independent. The independence of the judiciary should be protected – especially from the executive branch. Friend,
Yesterday, the Trump White House called me a _**“no-name Congresswoman”**_ and told me to _**“pivot away from freshman class antics.”**_
Why? Because a Social Security office in my district showed up on a federal closure list, and I fought to keep it open. Our community showed up, held multiple rallies, and we got the administration to back off.
Now, they’re trying to discredit me.
And honestly? That just tells me we hit a nerve.
The fact that President Trump and Elon Musk -- who called Social Security a “Ponzi scheme” -- are giving me grief should tell you everything you need to know. I’m fighting for working families, and they’re trying to shut me up.
I’m not bending the knee. I’m not backing down. And I sure as hell won’t apologize for standing up for working people in mid-Michigan.
**But they see our seat as vulnerable. MI-08 is a Trump district and a top target for Republicans in 2026. They’d love nothing more than to flip it back to send a message -- especially now.**

I have long, and proudly, worked on interfaith coalition building. When extremists attacked a Jewish cemetery near my mosque in Philadelphia, I was proud to activate my mosque community to help with clean up. When I was asked to speak at the funeral of a Holocaust Survivor and serve as a pallbearer, I considered it my distinct honor. Whenever I've been invited to Seders and Synagogues to break bread or speak on interfaith harmony, I've embraced the opportunities. These moments of unity and solidarity are important to a healthy society, in significant part because unfortunately, provocateurs have long tried to drive a wedge between Muslims and Jews with varying degrees of success.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f6cf0425-e6c1-4c6a-8470-91af5c1fc07d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Speaking at the funeral of a Holocaust survivor in 2018, in Richmond, VA.
And now, the Trump regime disappears and arrests immigrants, intimidates universities, and defunds programs under the guise of "combatting antisemitism." Meanwhile, Donald Trump proudly pardoned the Nazi who wore a "Camp Auschwitz" sweatshirt while storming the Capitol and beating cops to death--yet claims Mahmoud Khalil calling for justice for Jews and Palestinians alike is somehow antisemitic. Nonsense.
Trump is doing his best to create division and discord with disinformation and demonization, and joining him is a sustained campaign of misinformation. In this piece, I dive in to debunk a popular meme that is creating hate between Muslims and Jews. You may have seen it, but if not, I want you to have this information ahead of time. **Let 's Address This.**
**Earnest Ask!** I am doing everything in my power to stave off fascism in the United States, and I need your support. **Subscribe and join more than 130,000+ fellow activists.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..TqLNS2VLdrEAlhY52fzmyfSpfr7lPwC9ySCulqfvzwU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=162132878)
I received this meme from a Jewish friend. They sent it as a heads up and request to provide context for those who might fall victim to this dangerous misinformation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b664d9b1-ba95-4435-91d2-9b10c93e5b4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The meme depicts two women speaking to one another. The first woman says:
> "Isn't the Israeli Palestinian conflict just a Middle Eastern argument over land between Muslims and Jews?"
To which the second woman responds:
> "Yes, but not the first. Jewish people have lived in Jerusalem for thousands of years. And they've lived in the Middle East for ages, being oppressed, raped + murdered by the Arab Empire, like Palestinian Christians."
By the time I received this meme it had been shared thousands of times across social media, fueled by celebrities with large platforms. At a time of immense antisemitism and Islamophobia, such memes do nothing to advance peace and understanding, but create immense fear to advance hate and violence. They dangerously misrepresent history and create anti-Muslim hate and antisemitic hate--not to mention the total erasure of Palestinian Christians.
I launched Let's Address This to combat this type of disinformation and to instead uphold universal human rights. I want to ensure my readers have a reliable, trusted source from which to glean information and set the record straight.
So let's set the record straight.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..TqLNS2VLdrEAlhY52fzmyfSpfr7lPwC9ySCulqfvzwU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=162132878)
To do so, let's start from the beginning. In 622 C.E., the Founder of Islam, Prophet Muhammad, left Mecca after a dozen years of brutal persecution. He traveled some 220 miles by foot and arrived in Medina, a city state that was predominantly Jewish with a growing Muslim population. As part of the new government he helped establish, he ratified the landmark Constitution of Medina, sometimes known as the Charter of Medina. Established in 622, the Constitution of Medina was history's first secular Constitution. It mandated separation of religion and state and united the Muslims and Jews as one alliance. It comprised of 57 Articles, including these two gems most relevant to our discussion:
> **Article 17: No Jew shall be wronged for being a Jew.**
> **Article 18: The enemies of the Jews who follow [Muslims] will NOT be helped.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/afd82679-5f2a-4d24-b823-cdac04b34fea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Image of Charter of Medina
The Charter went on to explicitly confirm the humanity of Jewish people as equal to Muslims (Article 42), and the obligations of Muslims to protect not only Jews, but also allies of the Jews who were not explicitly mentioned in the Charter (Article 34). This ironclad commitment would soon be put to the test as war would impose itself on Medina. Accordingly, when Medina was subsequently attacked in the following years, for example in what is now known as the Battle of the Ditch, history records that Prophet Muhammad and the Muslims actively defended Jews from attack and being killed, and protected Medina's unified sovereignty and sanctity.
Meanwhile, some 600 miles away and six years later in 629, Byzantine Christians conquered Jerusalem and forcibly expelled all Jews from this holy city. A massacre of Jews ensued. Going forward, Jews were forbidden from settling in Jerusalem and were forced, by some accounts, to live at least 3 miles outside the city walls.
This atrocity against Jews was _not_ committed by Arabs or Muslims--as they had an alliance with Jews and remained steadfast in that alliance--but by the Byzantines.
**If you 're finding value in this scholarship, I invite you to join by subscribing.**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..TqLNS2VLdrEAlhY52fzmyfSpfr7lPwC9ySCulqfvzwU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=162132878)
Prophet Muhammad died in 632, and his death tested whether the alliance he made with Jews, and the promise of protection of Jews from harm, would remain in tact? That question was emphatically answered in 638 when the Caliph Umar conquered Jerusalem and retook it from the Byzantine Christians. As among his first orders of business, Umar reopened Jerusalem for Jews to reenter and live peacefully and without persecution. The restrictions in movement and residency that the Byzantines had imposed upon the Jewish people were also lifted. Likewise, Christians were allowed to remain in Jerusalem provided they did not engage in war. Subsequently, Jews, Muslims, and Christians live in relative peace under Muslim rule for the next 461 years. Soak that in for a moment. The United States has only existed for 249 years. But for nearly double the existence of the United States, Jews and Christians lived peacefully under Muslim rule in Jerusalem.
That unity continued until the Crusaders retook Jerusalem from the Muslims in 1099. Horrifyingly, another massacre ensued, again not committed by Arabs or Muslims, but _of_ Muslims and _of_ Jews at the hands of the Christian Crusaders.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25a0a7ef-452d-41fb-9799-53a1b40ee558?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From 1099-1187, the First Crusaders conquered Jerusalem and committed a well documented massacre of the previous Jewish and Muslim residents of Jerusalem.
And true to the Constitution of Medina signed some 467 years prior, Jews and Muslims fought side-by-side against the invading army, but lost. Those who survived the war were once again expelled from Jerusalem altogether. That is, until 1187. In 1187, General Saladin launched a successful campaign against the Crusaders and the Muslims retook Jerusalem, _again_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e171e4be-9e1d-4741-8ac7-7f18eda468c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And yet _again_ , true to the covenant established more than 500 years prior, General Saladin and the Muslims allowed Jews to re-enter Jerusalem, a second time, just as Caliph Omar had done centuries prior. He furthermore let native Christians remain in Jerusalem. And, as another token of his sincerity, he compassionately guarded the Holy Sepulcher of Christ from attack, vandalism, or destruction, honoring the Christian faith and its adherents. In 2022 I had the honor of visiting Jerusalem and seeing for myself, that to this day a Muslim family is the caretaker for the Holy Sepulcher, and ensures it remains open, clean, and free access to all who wish to visit.
All this contrary to the malicious allegation of "rape of Palestinian Christians." In fact, to this day in 2025, the Holy Sepulcher is honored under Muslim protection. When I had the honor of visiting the Holy Sepulcher and paying my respects personally, I was struck by the beauty of seeing Muslims, Jews, and Christians honoring the holy ground collectively and in peace.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/20fb7b35-f76c-4cc0-aaac-d18bee4955b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Top Left: Me standing before the Holy Sepulcher of Christ. Top Right: The building maintained by a Palestinian Muslim family that houses the Holy Sepulcher. Bottom: The stone slab upon which Jesus Christ is said to have been placed upon after the crucifixion. [Credit: My personal photos].
Again, to emphasize the point once more--what I observed was not new. Jews and Muslims (and Christians under Muslim and Jewish rule) lived in relative harmony and peace without any such incidents of "rape and murder by the Arab empire."
From 1259-1516, under the Mamluk reign, there were several notable Jews and Christians in high ranking positions in the Muslim majority government of Jerusalem. To be sure, this was not a utopia by any means, but likewise, there are no such examples of "mass murder or rape" as alleged. The Mamluk reign lasted until 1517, when the Ottomans took over Jerusalem.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..TqLNS2VLdrEAlhY52fzmyfSpfr7lPwC9ySCulqfvzwU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=162132878)
From 1517-1917, under 400 years of Muslim rule we once again history records relative peace and a rapid growth of the Jewish population in Jerusalem. This era amounted to the _third_ multi-century reign of Muslim leadership, in which Jews lived in Jerusalem, protected by Muslims from outside attacks, and free to practice and worship without oppression. This alone should suffice as evidence that Muslims and Jews have long lived in peace and harmony with one another.
And this harmony wasn't only in the Middle East.
Vastly contrary to the treatment of Jewish people under Christian Europe, in Moorish Spain we see 700 years of Muslim rule and relative peace between Muslims, Jews, and Christians. Indeed this was known as the Golden Age of Islam. As historian Gwendolyn Midlo Hall relates about this time period:

subject: Russia attacks Kyiv and how you can support AmeriCorps
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WITH HONOR ACTION, INC
body:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/1568ccaef30c/2-acts-and-a-vp-nominee-14052472?e=33f53a5b1a)
https://withhonor.org/
https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/air-defence-units-action-around-kyiv-officials-say-2025-04-23/
Friends,

Earlier this week, Russia launched its deadliest wave of attacks in nine months on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv. Ukrainian emergency services report that at least 12 people have died in the strikes, with 90 injured, and more casualties are likely to be trapped under the rubble as search and rescue efforts continue. Underscoring the brutality of the Russian invasion, Moscow sent 70 missiles and 145 drones toward Ukraine, striking 13 civilian locations in Kyiv.

Just a few days before this attack, Representative Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) visited Ukraine, meeting with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine, Bridget Brink, in Kyiv. As the co-chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus and co-founder of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Rep. Fitzpatrick is one of the most bipartisan Members of Congress and has a background service in the FBI. We were proud to be with him in Ukraine, and you can hear more about his trip from his interview with Face the Nation.
https://www.cbsnews.com/news/brian-fitzpatrick-ukraine-face-the-nation-transcript-04-20-2025/
📺 You can watch the full interview here (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/brian-fitzpatrick-ukraine-face-the-nation-transcript-04-20-2025/) .
https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2025/04/23/americorps-congress-trump-cuts/
“It’s a selfless act to serve, but you are gaining experience, and you are able to parlay that into opportunities in the civilian economy,” Rep. Chrissy Houlahan said, an Air Force veteran who served in Teach for America in Philadelphia through AmeriCorps.
Over the past few weeks, Members of Congress have launched a bipartisan, bicameral push to save AmeriCorps, whose staff was cut by about 75%. As people who know the value of service to our country, the veteran members of the bipartisan For Country Caucus (https://ellzey.house.gov/for-country-caucus) have led the way in this fight. Representatives Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA) and Don Bacon (R-NE), both Air Force veterans, sent a letter to President Trump last week, urging him to work with Congress not to take unilateral action that can hurt service in America and to work with Congress to reform and modernize AmeriCorps.
https://houlahan.house.gov/uploadedfiles/04.10.2025_letter_on_americorps_reform.pdf
And the dismantling of AmeriCorps has already made its effects felt.

➡️ Noe Felix Burns, an AmeriCorps NCCC member, was at a worksite in Pennsylvania helping repair homes damaged by Hurricane Ida in 2021. He told Colorado Public Radio (https://www.cpr.org/2025/04/22/trump-americorps-program-cuts/) , “I thought our site supervisor was joking until he told us. We asked him, ‘Should we finish cleaning up?’ He's like, ‘No, get your stuff. We got to go now.’ And then he called the homeowner over and started telling her, apologizing to her that we wouldn't be able to finish the work.”

➡️ In Wisconsin, teams of AmeriCorps NCCC members were scheduled to build homes, be camp counselors for a "sibling camp" that brings together children separated by foster care, and clear trails. Jennifer Johnson tells the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel (https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/2025/04/17/doge-cuts-to-americorps-mean-wisconsin-projects-lose-volunteers/83128638007/?emci=a7c73f98-7d1c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=4b386572-881c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=13328754) that "We are at this point in time, just not even 24 hours into the announcement, pivoting and regrouping and trying to come up with Plan B. And I don't know what that will be yet."
How You Can Help
Only a few weeks ago, With Honor Action was proud to celebrate the fifth anniversary of the National Commission on Military, National, and Public Service's "Inspire to Serve" report, which proposed a blueprint to make service, both military and non-military, a cornerstone of American democracy.

Today, we remain committed to that ideal. Working with our partners at Voices for National Service, here are some easy things you can do to support AmeriCorps.

1. Take one minute to send an email to your Member of Congress (https://click.everyaction.com/k/106086828/540379087/979679100?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwNDI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YjM4NjU3Mi04ODFjLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImxlQHdpdGhob25vci5vcmciDQp9&hmac=_s1568JP-fECNN76_RvNyu_DK3FG9iv1km-EoIJUJ5s=&emci=a7c73f98-7d1c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=4b386572-881c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=13328754) , we promise it works to hear from constituents!

2. Place a call to your lawmakers and ask them to protect AmeriCorps. We have instructions and a sample script you can use (https://click.everyaction.com/k/106086829/540379088/309696662?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwNDI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YjM4NjU3Mi04ODFjLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImxlQHdpdGhob25vci5vcmciDQp9&hmac=_s1568JP-fECNN76_RvNyu_DK3FG9iv1km-EoIJUJ5s=&emci=a7c73f98-7d1c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=4b386572-881c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=13328754) .

3. Encourage others to get involved and use their voice by sharing some of our draft social media posts (https://click.everyaction.com/k/106086830/540379089/406981918?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwNDI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YjM4NjU3Mi04ODFjLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImxlQHdpdGhob25vci5vcmciDQp9&hmac=_s1568JP-fECNN76_RvNyu_DK3FG9iv1km-EoIJUJ5s=&emci=a7c73f98-7d1c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=4b386572-881c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=13328754#act-now-protect-americorps) and downloadable graphics.

4. Share your AmeriCorps alumni story (https://click.everyaction.com/k/106086831/540379090/321592954?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwNDI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YjM4NjU3Mi04ODFjLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImxlQHdpdGhob25vci5vcmciDQp9&hmac=_s1568JP-fECNN76_RvNyu_DK3FG9iv1km-EoIJUJ5s=&emci=a7c73f98-7d1c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=4b386572-881c-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=13328754) with the Service Year Alliance to help showcase the benefits of AmeriCorps.

Thank you for standing with us, with AmeriCorps, and with all Americans who have chosen or may choose to serve our nation, in any capacity.

Some of you may have read that dozens of Brooklyn residents set up tents to protest a homeless shelter. This is actually a physical structure to be set up. These protesters set up shelters covered in American flags with protest signs. [See NY Post](https://substack.com/redirect/03a7cc0f-6318-4d2e-9b52-b99fb8fe35e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

---|---|---
Here in Connecticut, we're not even building shelters, which are a humane and a logical way to temporarily address these issues as we determine permanent residence or places of permanent shelter.

Instead, our genius state has raised Bill Number 7033 which prohibits "any municipality from imposing any penalty on homeless persons for performing life, sustaining activities on public land." **This got out of the Housing Committee of 20 with 14 in favor, 4 in opposition (Courpas, Sampson, Jensen, Weir) and 2 Absent - It could hit the floor and with a Dem controlled Statehouse - your summer areas of recreation could become tent cities.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d463879-2806-4124-9a23-c0f7e60b6a2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

**What is public land?**
Well it's "any property that's owned or lease by any state or local government entity or any property where there's an easement for public use and held open to the public on any federal land where local law-enforcement has jurisdiction to enforce loss including courtyard, public lot, sidewalks, public transportation facilities, and services, public buildings, shopping centers, underpasses, and land adjacent to roadways and parks."
GREAT - SHOPPING CENTERS ARE NOW PUBLIC EVEN THOUGH THEY ARE PRIVATELY OWNED AND MAINTAINED

[Pledge your support](https://substack..R8E7tMNeah6FCNjaNhMihoT6ZZmnDAEuwmJsaSvauk8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=162134617)
This is as ridiculous as watching the senior couple in the movie Caddyshack as his wife hits a golf ball into a pond and the husband gives her an attaboy and utters "That's a peach hon." **There 's nothing peachy about this bill.
**
As far as life sustaining activities, this includes " moving resting, sitting, standing, lying down, sleeping protecting out from the elements, eating drinking and storing such personal property as needed to safely shelter oneself."

What's also allowed is "to be free from civil or criminal sanctions for soliciting sharing, accepting or offering food water, money or other donations in public places."

It also assesses a civil penalty on any person or municipality, which would include the police for any offense. And the AG can institute a civil action. Another opportunity for AG Tong to hit the soapbox at his next Indivisible rally.

**You ask what you can do?
**
If you have a State rep or State senator that lives in your district and they have a sidewalk in front of their house, maybe it's time as the Doobie Brothers said to take it to the streets - Maybe you set up camp in front of their house.
**Also - Share this with every supermarket you know and and shopping center owner - let them know.** _They will get a lot of the traffic from this as the panhandling will also be easier there._

Why cant we learn from those mistakes and the ones from California which is three years ahead of us in horrendous legislation with unintended consequences.

Real solutions and assistance is needed here and advocates to end homelessness asked for $33.5 million for the homeless crisis in CT in which the Coalition to end Homelessness indicated there were less than 1000 people living outside (as of February 2025). This request is to fund eviction prevention rental assistance, homelessness response services in case management for permanent supportive housing.

While the endgame of this legislation is unclear, some of the homelessness in this state is a result of un affordability in housing and in other aspects, especially utilities, which continue to be on the rise (with a minor break coming).
Connecticut has some of the highest utility rates in the country with ample access to sufficient energy generation.
Yet this public benefits that we continue to discuss is a major source of some of these housing costs to our Connecticut residents.
**Connecticut has to become more affordable.**

Just watch as this homeless debate becomes something to expand the discussion into more transit oriented development, massive expansion of 8-30g and public housing plans that are poorly designed to meet the actual needs of a community.

name: Rep. Joe Sweeney
subject: The Fight for New Hampshire’s Future Starts Now
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Granite Solutions
body:
Grateful to be in this fight.
| | | | [](https://link.emails.granitesolutions.)
---

Derek,
As Granite Staters, we pride ourselves on doing things differently—and doing them right. We believe in personal responsibility, limited government, and the idea that our future should be built from the ground up by the people who live and work here, not dictated by Washington or out-of-touch elites.
That’s the spirit I carry with me every time I'm at the State House. And that’s the spirit that drives our agenda for New Hampshire.
We’ve come a long way, but the truth is clear: our way of life is under pressure. Out-of-state interests, progressive activists, and national political operatives are pouring in with one goal—to reshape New Hampshire in their image. They want to grow government, weaken our institutions, and erase the values that define our state. We can’t let that happen.
That’s why now, more than ever, we need to stand together. Not just to defend what makes New Hampshire great—but to go on offense and fight for a stronger, freer, safer future.

### **Here’s what I’m working to deliver:**

**Lower Taxes and a Stronger Economy:**
Families and small businesses are getting crushed by inflation and bad federal policies. In Concord, we’re cutting taxes, streamlining government, and supporting job creators so that more families can thrive and more young people can afford to build a life right here in New Hampshire.
**Safe Streets and Strong Communities:**
We’re taking a stand against the fentanyl crisis, pushing back on the idea of sanctuary policies, and giving law enforcement the tools they need to keep our neighborhoods safe. That includes fighting to end catch-and-release practices and making sure dangerous criminals are off the streets.
**Parental Rights and Quality Education:**
I believe parents—not bureaucrats—should be in charge of their children’s education. That means promoting transparency in the classroom, expanding education freedom, and making sure every child—regardless of ZIP code—has the opportunity to succeed.
**Protecting Our Values:**
The New Hampshire Advantage isn’t just a slogan—it’s a commitment to personal liberty, local control, and fiscal responsibility. We’re leading the charge to preserve what makes our state unique, from protecting free speech and the Second Amendment to ensuring our elections remain secure and trustworthy.
This is more than a legislative agenda—it’s a call to action. Because we know that real change doesn’t start in the halls of government—it starts with people like you.
You don’t have to be elected to make a difference. Every letter, every phone call, every conversation with a neighbor matters. When citizens speak up, elected officials listen. When communities come together, change happens.
So I’m asking you to stay engaged. Advocate for our values. Tell your story. Support leaders who put New Hampshire first. And never forget that in this state, the people still have the power.
We’re going to keep fighting every day—for our economy, our families, our freedoms, and our future. And with your voice behind us, I know we’ll keep New Hampshire on the right path.
Thank you for standing strong. Thank you for believing in our mission. And thank you for being part of this effort to protect the place we all call home.
In service,
**Rep. Joe Sweeney**
Chairman, Granite Solutions

name: Josh Harder
subject: What I heard at my town hall
body:
Lots of anger. I get it.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106500069/541708256/-1860252395?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTBhNGQ2NTktZWUyMS1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=72bOpp8JJo29MZ_qXjCVetKyrImyOqPUpAy--9wRgcQ=) | Peter, This week I held a town hall in my district’s largest city, Stockton. It was an overflow crowd - over 300 people attended to share their thoughts and ideas about how we can fight back against what’s going on in D.C. I thought you’d be interested in my abbreviated notes from the event:
* People are very concerned about Donald Trump + Elon Musk’s unconstitutional efforts to dismantle our government.
* Trump’s tariffs are killing people’s 401k’s and they are livid we may be headed into a recession
* Social security and Medicare were huge topics - people very worried about the GOP slashing of benefits

I’ll tell you what I told them: I’m also livid and scared and frustrated. We need to channel these feelings into _effective_ action. We need to ignore the noise and focus on how we can push back in an organized way (ex. litigation, force the media to pay attention, use Appropriations process to fight back). Democrats also need to be holding more town halls - not only does it give people a chance to gather and organize, but **it highlights how scared Republicans are to face their voters.** I’m proud to be one of the most accessible Members of Congress. For me, it’s simple - if you aren’t willing to listen to your voters, you shouldn’t be in office. Right now, Congressional Republicans know they can’t defend their positions to voters, so they aren’t even trying. They need to be held accountable. Thanks to everyone who attended our town hall. We have a lot of work to do, and I’m constantly inspired by this team’s energy and determination. \- Josh
---

body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
In our previous edition we warned about the slippery slope we were in when it came to deportations.
Since, the Trump regime has wrongly detained dozens of U.S. citizens — including a ten-year-old Texas girl [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/us-citizen-child-recovering-brain-cancer-deported-mexico-undocumented-rcna196049] recovering from brain cancer, a 19-year-old U.S. citizen with learning disabilities who was [https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/04/us-citizen-jose-hermosillo-wrongly-detained-ice-patrol-governments-account-false/?fbclid=IwY2xjawJ2Qi9leHRuA2FlbQIxMQBicmlkETFPbU5wOTFVREhWYktoNnc5AR7Fe9oVKjamHuG3WmhfyvfnCRNedF3MORvKe81-https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/04/us-citizen-jose-hermosillo-wrongly-detained-ice-patrol-governments-account-false/] wrongfully incarcerated [https://popular.info/p/federal-immigration-authorities-wrongfully] for 10 days in a privately run immigration detention facility in Arizona or a 20-year-old born in Georgia [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/us-born-citizen-detained-ice-immigration-florida-rcna201800] , and arrested in Florida.
All mistakes, that cause fear in the American population. The deportation of Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, who, due to an “administrative error,” was sent to a dangerous and violent mega-prison in El Salvador, does not help ease the fear.
The Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments to the Constitution [https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/due_process] establish the right to due process — the Fifth Amendment says that “[n]o person shall ... be deprived of life, liberty, or property, without due process of law.” The Fourteenth Amendment extends this obligation to the states.
No PERSON. This is true even for the undocumented, even if someone is here without authorization.
Due process for Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, should have included notice of deportation and the opportunity to contest it before it happened. Now even as the Supreme Court has ruled for his return, he has yet to be returned home
We remember Fannie Lou Hamer's statement: "No one is free until everyone is free," which is more relevant today than ever.
REGISTER TO VOTE [https://vote.pa/check/?org=nppef]
Social Media of the Week
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Screenshot%202025-04-24%20110558.png] "I'll tell you what freedom is to me: no fear." – Nina Simone
Nina Simone was a classically trained pianist (not common for a young Black woman in the 1950s) who fused her foundation with jazz, gospel, blues, and folk to create a sound entirely her own, defying all genres.
She didn’t fit into a box or label, nor did she try to.
Simone was denied entry to a prestigious music school, the Curtis Institute of Music in Philadelphia, because of her race. This moment fueled her lifelong work in civil rights.
Her songs like “Mississippi Goddam” became an anthem for civil rights and Black empowerment nationally.
"An artist's duty is to reflect the times." – Nina Simone

The U.S. Justice Department withdrew its lawsuit [https://triblive.com/news/pennsylvania/justice-department-drops-lawsuit-accusing-pennsylvania-city-of-diluting-power-of-hispanic-voters/] that accused the heavily Hispanic city of Hazleton in Pennsylvania of illegally diluting the political power of its growing Hispanic population. The department’s initial lawsuit, filed in January, said the “at-large” system of electing city council members, as opposed to electing them by district, was unfair to Hispanic voters and prevented them from getting elected to city council. Hazleton’s 30,000 residents are about two-thirds Hispanic, according to U.S. Census figures. One-third is non-Hispanic white.
Closer to Philadelphia, the largest health system in Delaware County began closing two hospitals [https://6abc.com/post/crozer-health-hospital-emergency-rooms-stop-accepting-patients/16228691/] Wednesday after a federal judge in Texas approved their bankruptcy proceedings. The emergency rooms of Taylor Hospital in Ridley Park and Crozer-Chester Medical Center in Upland are expected to close today, Friday, April 25th. Emergency medical services will end next Friday, on May 2. Crozer's ambulatory centers at Brinton Lakes, Broomall, Haverford, and Media are expected to remain open.

State Rep. David Rowe (R-Union) wants to introduce a bill to make it easier for hunters and fishermen to get registered to vote [https://www.palegis.us/house/co-sponsorship/memo?memoID=46210] . He represents a lot of sportsmen in the rural 85th state House District, which includes parts of Union, Juniata, and Mifflin counties and all of Snyder County.
“The bill will not complicate the process of getting a license. The bill will not add another step to the hunting license process,” Rowe told Capital-Star [https://penncapital-star.com/government-politics/general-assembly/state-rep-david-rowe-wants-to-make-it-easier-for-sportsmen-to-register-to-vote/] . “Rather, it will simply make it more accessible. So, for sportsmen that are going to a state office, there will be paper registration forms available for them to simply grab.”
As a voting rights organization, we applaud all legislation that would make it easier for people to register to vote, and make our voices to be heard at the ballot box.
Meanwhile, Pennsylvania’s first two openly autistic legislators, State Reps. They are also opposed to his plan to collect private medical records from US citizens to research autism. Remember that slippery slope regarding immigrant deportations?
And if you are waiting for a tax return but have defaulted student loans, there is a chance the government will garnish your return and even your wages. The Department of Education announced Monday it will restart collections on defaulted federal student loans on May 5 [https://thehill.com/homenews/education/5259465-education-department-defaulted-federal-student-loans-debt-collection-trump-mcmahon] , including potentially garnishing wages for millions of workers. The Treasury Offset Program allows the government to withhold federal payments such as tax returns for individuals in default. After a 30-day notice, the federal government could also begin garnishing a borrower’s wages. So make sure to check your statement.

Friends,
As promised, I wanted to share more updates directly with you on what I’ve been doing to fight back against Trump and what you can do too. I am going to try to send these every other Friday — so let me know if you have any feedback, what you like (or what you don’t like), and what you want to see!
3 things I did in the past two weeks to push back against Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and House Republicans:
1. I traveled to Iraq, Bahrain, Qatar, and the UAE to meet with regional partners and stand up for our values abroad. The Trump Administration has continued to green-light arms sales to the UAE, despite their direct involvement in Sudan’s violent civil war. I spoke directly to Emirati officials and condemned their continued support for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan, which is fueling genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and ethnic cleansing, and exacerbating a humanitarian crisis impacting more than 30 million people. Trump is abdicating our responsibilities and leadership on the world stage, but I’ve introduced the Stand Up for Sudan Act with Senator Chris Van Hollen that would prohibit U.S. arms sales to the UAE until they stop providing material support to the RSF.
2. I hosted another town hall, talking directly to hundreds of my constituents for two hours. This was my third town hall of the year, and it was energizing to hear from so many folks in our community who are concerned, engaged, and ready to fight back. I was also grateful that a number of my Republican constituents came out and asked their questions. We won’t always see eye to eye, but honest conversations with folks we disagree with is one of the biggest ways to rebuild trust and strengthen our community.
3. I met with local Jewish community leaders to hear about their concerns under the Trump Administration — from the frozen funding of FEMA’s Nonprofit Security Grants that protect our synagogues and other at-risk community spaces and the defunding of the Office of Civil Rights that investigates instances of antisemitism. These are serious concerns that will devastate the Jewish community and so many others. More on this soon.
3 things you can do to fight back and make a difference in your community:
1. Check on your neighbors and make sure they know their rights if they ever encounter federal law enforcement. The ACLU has resources in English and Spanish [https://www.aclu.org/know-your-rights/immigrants-rights] that outline the rights people are guaranteed under the Constitution, regardless of immigration status — share them widely!
2. Call Republican Members of Congress to sign onto H.R. 2601, the Delete DOGE Act . I’ve heard privately from so many of my Republican colleagues that they are horrified by the deep, unstrategic, and harmful slash and burn tactics from Elon Musk’s DOGE. But it’s time for them to go public. I introduced the Delete DOGE Act to rescind and prohibit the use of federal funds for DOGE. You can call the U.S. House switchboard at (202) 224-3121 to speak to Republican Members of Congress and urge them to join the bill.
3. In San Diego? Attend CBFD Indivisible’s monthly meeting on Sunday, April 27. I’ll be there and taking questions from folks who attend. I’ve heard there’s limited space left, so sign up now to try to grab a spot [https://www.mobilize.us/cbfd-indivisible/event/776563/] !
3 pieces of good news:
1. The Department of Defense released guidance stating that trans and gender non-binary service members can once again receive gender affirming health care! This guidance follows the second ruling from a federal district court judge that blocked the Trump Administration’s discriminatory trans military ban.
2. A federal district court judge ruled that President Trump illegally invoked the Alien Enemies Act , the 1798 law that Trump has been using to legitimize mass deportations without due process.
3. Republican Congressman Don Bacon called for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to be fired over his reckless lack of leadership and judgment. We need good faith Republican leaders to speak up and speak out about the dangerous behavior from the Trump Administration. Congressman Bacon is one of the first to do it, and it’s a big deal.
I hope this was helpful and hopeful. As always, let me know if there’s anything else you’d like to hear about in the next few weeks.
Warmly,
Sara

The ACLU has resources in English and Spanish [] that outline the rights people are guaranteed under the Constitution, regardless of immigration status — share them widely! 2. Call Republican Members of Congress to sign onto H.R. 2601, the Delete DOGE Act . I’ve heard privately from so many of my Republican colleagues that they are horrified by the deep, unstrategic, and harmful slash and burn tactics from Elon Musk’s DOGE. But it’s time for them to go public. I introduced the Delete DOGE Act to rescind and prohibit the use of federal funds for DOGE. You can call the U.S. House switchboard at (202) 224-3121 to speak to Republican Members of Congress and urge them to join the bill. 3. In San Diego? Attend CBFD Indivisible’s monthly meeting on Sunday, April 27. I’ll be there and taking questions from folks who attend. I’ve heard there’s limited space left, so sign up now to try to grab a spot [] ! 3 pieces of good news: 1. The Department of Defense released guidance stating that trans and gender non-binary service members can once again receive gender affirming health care! This guidance follows the second ruling from a federal district court judge that blocked the Trump Administration’s discriminatory trans military ban. 2. A federal district court judge ruled that President Trump illegally invoked the Alien Enemies Act , the 1798 law that Trump has been using to legitimize mass deportations without due process. 3. Republican Congressman Don Bacon called for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to be fired over his reckless lack of leadership and judgment. We need good faith Republican leaders to speak up and speak out about the dangerous behavior from the Trump Administration. Congressman Bacon is one of the first to do it, and it’s a big deal. I hope this was helpful and hopeful. As always, let me know if there’s anything else you’d like to hear about in the next few weeks. clean_body: | | | | | Hi Friend, Welcome to this special edition of the New Pennsylvania Project newsletter!In this special edition of our newsletter, we highlight all the good trouble from the last few weeks. We also invite you to join us at some of our upcoming events.Remember Pennsylvanians vote twice a year, every year! | | | | | | | Primary Election Information Session On Saturday, April 26, 2025, from 1:30 to 4pm, join our founding CEO at an information session about the upcoming primary election on Tuesday, May 20th. The info session is hosted by NPP and the Wynnefield Community Neighborhood Association (WCNA).The event will take place at Mingle Event Studio, 1905 N. 54th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19131. This event is great for folks who need some guidance on how to vote in a judicial election - especially first time voters! | | | | School Director Candidate Virtual Forum On Monday, April 28th, our founding CEO will join the Montgomery County Chapter of the Democratic Black Caucus & Parents For Inclusion for a virtual school board forum.Kadida Kenner will moderate the debate for the candidates for two of the six districts: Upper Perk & Cheltenham. The virtual forum will take place from 6pm to 8:30 pm on zoom. Have a question for the candidates? You can fill out the Community Question Form when you register for the event using the link below. | | | | | Episode 2 of aired on Thursday, April 24th at noon! Kadida opens with the story of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Maryland father wrongfully deported to El Salvador and detained in one of the world’s most notorious prisons. Gracia remains detained in El Salvador despite a U.S. Supreme Court ruling calling for his return. Kadida then shares her recent experience at a protest where someone told her to "go back to Africa," leading to a larger conversation about the power of protest, Black identity, and diaspora pride. Listen to us where you get your podcasts: , , , , and . Plus, watch us on | Why Courts Matter with Indivisible Greater Jenkintown | | On April 19th, our founding CEO highlighted just how important the upcoming judicial elections are for the future of Pennsylvania. At the event hosted byIndivisible Greater Jenkintown , talked about the importance of volunteering and the impact individuals can have on election outcomes. | | | | Hands Off protests | | Dr. Kimeka Campbell speaks at the Harrisburg event | | Kadida Kenner in Philadelphia | | Both our founding CEO and our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement, Dr. Kimeka Campbel l spoke at Hands Off protests, a series of demonstrations launched across the country. Participation is the foundation of a strong democracy. When people understand how government works, what their rights are, and how to engage in the political process, they’re more empowered to vote—and to vote with purpose. | On April 22nd, 2025, Idavox published an article titled: “Go Back To Africa!” Judge’s Son Harasses Rally Participants in Pennsylvania With Racist Slur. subject: Donald Trump’s “peace deal” will only lead to more war
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
He’s embracing the same predatory posture that led to two world wars and hundreds of thousands of dead Americans.
#
Peter, Alex Vindman here.
Donald Trump and JD Vance are demanding Ukraine take their most recent “peace deal” or they will cut and run. So, let’s get into it. What’s in this deal?
Formal recognition of Russian control in Crimea. Formal recognition of Russian control of virtually all occupied Ukrainian territory. Forbidding Ukraine from joining NATO. Lifting all sanctions imposed on Russia since their illegal occupation of Crimea. Forging new economic ties between the U.S. and Russia.
This is the same extortion scheme Trump tried and I reported him for, resulting in the first impeachment — a demand Zelenskyy do what Trump wants or Ukraine is cut off.
This “peace deal” is Russia’s deal, maximum pain for Ukraine and maximum reward for Russia. It abandons Ukraine and Europe and is a gift to Russia. It sends a clear message to the world’s tyrants: They can invade, terrorize, murder, and be rewarded rather than punished for it.
I wrote the Crimea Declaration in Trump’s first term when I worked on the National Security Council, which made it the position of the United States to recognize Crimea as Ukrainian land and reject Russia’s illegal occupation. Trump 2.0, now completely unchecked, abandons it. He’s embracing the same predatory posture that led to two world wars and hundreds of thousands of dead Americans.
Trump and Putin share that predatory world view, and it won’t make America wealthier. It won’t make us safer. It will make the world a more dangerous place and put American troops at risk.
I refuse to stand by as Trump takes us down this path, and I’m proud to work with VoteVets as they hold him accountable and combat his administration.
[**Can you add your name and say that you’re with us? Millions of Americans still stand with Ukraine, and speaking together in one voice sends a powerful message to Trump, Putin, and the entire world.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250425_ukraine/?source=em250425-1-120&akid=34373%2E3013755%2ELzhrV_)

Lt. Col. Alexander Vindman
U.S. Army, Ret.

Peter, it's Valerie –

Every Sunday morning, I go to church to pray.

name: Rep. Joe Sweeney
subject: The Fight for New Hampshire’s Future Starts Now
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Granite Solutions
body:
Grateful to be in this fight.
| | | | [](https://link.emails.granitesolutions.)
---

Derek,
As Granite Staters, we pride ourselves on doing things differently—and doing them right. We believe in personal responsibility, limited government, and the idea that our future should be built from the ground up by the people who live and work here, not dictated by Washington or out-of-touch elites.
That’s the spirit I carry with me every time I'm at the State House. And that’s the spirit that drives our agenda for New Hampshire.
We’ve come a long way, but the truth is clear: our way of life is under pressure. Out-of-state interests, progressive activists, and national political operatives are pouring in with one goal—to reshape New Hampshire in their image. They want to grow government, weaken our institutions, and erase the values that define our state. We can’t let that happen.
That’s why now, more than ever, we need to stand together. Not just to defend what makes New Hampshire great—but to go on offense and fight for a stronger, freer, safer future.

### **Here’s what I’m working to deliver:**

**Lower Taxes and a Stronger Economy:**
Families and small businesses are getting crushed by inflation and bad federal policies. In Concord, we’re cutting taxes, streamlining government, and supporting job creators so that more families can thrive and more young people can afford to build a life right here in New Hampshire.
**Safe Streets and Strong Communities:**
We’re taking a stand against the fentanyl crisis, pushing back on the idea of sanctuary policies, and giving law enforcement the tools they need to keep our neighborhoods safe. That includes fighting to end catch-and-release practices and making sure dangerous criminals are off the streets.
**Parental Rights and Quality Education:**
I believe parents—not bureaucrats—should be in charge of their children’s education. That means promoting transparency in the classroom, expanding education freedom, and making sure every child—regardless of ZIP code—has the opportunity to succeed.
**Protecting Our Values:**
The New Hampshire Advantage isn’t just a slogan—it’s a commitment to personal liberty, local control, and fiscal responsibility. We’re leading the charge to preserve what makes our state unique, from protecting free speech and the Second Amendment to ensuring our elections remain secure and trustworthy.
This is more than a legislative agenda—it’s a call to action. Because we know that real change doesn’t start in the halls of government—it starts with people like you.
You don’t have to be elected to make a difference. Every letter, every phone call, every conversation with a neighbor matters. When citizens speak up, elected officials listen. When communities come together, change happens.
So I’m asking you to stay engaged. Advocate for our values. Tell your story. Support leaders who put New Hampshire first. And never forget that in this state, the people still have the power.
We’re going to keep fighting every day—for our economy, our families, our freedoms, and our future. And with your voice behind us, I know we’ll keep New Hampshire on the right path.
Thank you for standing strong. Thank you for believing in our mission. And thank you for being part of this effort to protect the place we all call home.
In service,
**Rep. Joe Sweeney**
Chairman, Granite Solutions
[Donate Today](https://link.emails.granitesolutions.)

This is how change happens.
#
Hey, Sarah McBride here.
Last weekend, I joined the hosts of Pod Save America for a conversation about where we go from here — and what it means to show up in this moment.
At one point, they asked me:
_“Do you have advice for people in this moment who might be horrified by what they're seeing, but a little scared?”_
**Well, my dad used to say that if everyone has just a little bit of courage, then no one has to be a hero.**
It might be scary, but the more that everyday people speak out, the more that elected officials and other leaders will have the courage to speak out, too.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/25/2025
body:
Court sides with new Colorado GOP Chair, blocks committee tied to former leadership
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sdne438ff23)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3i045e82e5)**
| | Hi folks,
Listen to today's **Mountain Minute Podcast** [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/seu00074660), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s8j0ff536f5) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s5p69cd9ca6)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Colorado Legislative Session Updates...** HB1303 would fund a new "transportation enterprise" through [fees on car insurance](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sfvbb6bb341)—but instead of fixing roads, the money goes to projects like reducing bike and wildlife collisions. A separate measure, SB280, would give tech giants [millions in tax breaks](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s8o77662ac7) to build data centers—prompting pushback from watchdogs who say it trades away taxpayer funds without clear returns.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A judge backed GOP Chair Brita Horn, [blocking a committee](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s2s29da379c) tied to former leadership from pursuing party lawsuits. Valor Christian launched a [Turning Point USA chapter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/scna74ff6ef), rallying students around conservative values. As [Colorado tightens gun laws](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/san65ff75e2), Montana’s governor is urging firearm makers to relocate. Meanwhile, ICE plans to [double jail bed capacity](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s8q2803f832) in the metro area to meet rising enforcement needs.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** Wall Street rallied for a [third straight day](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sbqb6a7765f) as Trump signaled a softer tone on China tariffs, calming investor nerves. Alphabet (Google) earnings are also in focus as tech stocks drive the market rebound.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** C.J. Garbo blasts Democrats for [defending violent illegal immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s9hbd872c21) while targeting January 6 defendants, arguing equal justice is dead. Another commentary exposes Colorado’s broken mental health system, where kids in crisis face tragic delays—especially around [gender-affirming care](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/set7a5c9a63).
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, April 25, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Court sides with new Colorado GOP Chair, blocks committee tied to former leadership](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sflfe13a6c2)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sbr47cf714e)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s6j4731f6e0)
A district judge in El Paso County has rejected an attempt by the Colorado Republican Party’s Investigative Committee—an entity formed under former chair Dave Williams—to intervene in a lawsuit that the party’s current leadership has moved to dismiss.
In a ruling filed April 23, District Court Judge Amanda J. Philipps found that the Investigative Committee lacks standing and legal authority to join or intervene in the ongoing civil case, saying the group was assigned “limited tasks” and does not possess independent power to act on behalf of the Colorado Republican State Central Committee (CRC).
“Absent an express statutory right, a subordinate state agency lacks standing or any other legal authority to obtain judicial review of an action of a superior state agency,” the court stated, citing precedent from Ad Hoc Exec. Comm. v. Runyan.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s2g71ca6a74)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s7ka5861a0c)
|
---
**[Turning Point USA launches at Valor Christian: Courage, character, and a little wild West spirit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3j39932ea9)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s2qb921c801)
* Nearly 50 students, faculty, and guests gathered to launch a new high school chapter of Turning Point USA. The event opened with prayer and focused on freedom, courage, and conservative values.
* Aurora Councilwoman Danielle Jurinsky and former Denver Bronco Derek Wolfe addressed students, encouraging quiet strength and bold leadership. Wolfe told students, “Be a wolf or a lion, not a sheep.”
* TPUSA’s Gabby Reichardt emphasized the group’s growing national high school strategy, noting the strong participation of young women at Valor and the broader push to make political conversation fun, not polarizing.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3h202e3798)**
|
---
**[Garbo: How Democrats weaponized–and betrayed American citizens while defending criminal illegal immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/scr57b69c5b)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s6od2d051fb)
* C.J. Garbo argues Democrats offer more legal protection to violent illegal immigrants, like MS-13 members, than to U.S. citizens—particularly January 6 defendants, who he says were denied basic constitutional rights.
* Garbo claims Democrats have weaponized the justice system to punish political opponents while shielding criminal non-citizens, undermining the rule of law and public trust.
* The piece warns that continued betrayal of American citizens in favor of political narratives threatens the foundation of democracy and demands direct confrontation of these policies.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3n2dd14b91)**
|
---
**[Gimelshteyn: The unraveling medical crisis that Colorado parents must pay attention to](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s2i6bca5aae)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3m71b22080)
* The state’s pediatric crisis care is overwhelmed, with children waiting weeks or months for care. Many are placed in psychiatric holds for minor issues, leading to trauma and instability instead of healing.
* Gimelshteyn highlights cases where children with mental health struggles were pushed toward gender transition treatments without full psychological evaluations or adequate parental involvement.
* The piece urges lawmakers and medical institutions to slow down, prioritize full mental health assessments, and involve families—warning that politicized care is putting vulnerable children at risk.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s0vd8e4abc4)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Colorado law limits what voters can verify—and critics say that needs to change](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s6r4f72a492)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sajb53643a2)****BY JEN SCHUMANN****| STATE | APRIL 23** _Mesa County’s Ballot Verifier tool has been praised for giving residents unprecedented access to redacted ballot images and cast vote records. But for some longtime election integrity advocates, it’s only part of the solution._
**[From critics to champions: How a ballot transparency tool won over Idaho voters—and inspired Mesa County](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s5v4d072e84)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s4lf8b7940c)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | NATIONAL | APRIL 23** _When Ada County launched a ballot audit tool built by a small independent company, no one knew what to expect. But what followed surprised even the clerk who helped shape it._
**[Mesa County launches Ballot Verifier, giving voters unprecedented access to ballots](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s4i33ff3285)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3l6e63f2e7)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | APRIL 23** _Mesa County launched a first-of-its-kind ballot transparency tool last month, allowing residents to view redacted ballot images and corresponding cast vote records online—without filing a CORA request. Supporters say it could reshape public trust in elections. Others say it doesn’t go far enough._

**🐫 DID YOU KNOW?** The U.S. Army once experimented with **camels as pack animals** in the Southwest. In 1855, Congress approved $30,000 to import camels for use in the arid terrain of newly acquired territories. The experiment showed promise, but the Civil War disrupted the effort—and with many camel advocates siding with the Confederacy, the post-war Union shut the program down. Within a decade, most of the camels were sold off to circuses, zoos, and traveling shows.

name: Mark Warner
subject: I went down to Southwest Virginia
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Mark Warner
body:
let’s talk about speaking to people across lines of difference

|
---

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106508371/541734215/1894416887?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Nascar_250425_T1_1_b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTgyNDUwZC1mYjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JN322evRPfjOEgi3YiYj2V7pfy7-6bYC72uyXrVQlDE=) Derek,

Last week, I went back to Southwest Virginia, an area of our Commonwealth where I’ve always loved spending time.

While I was there, I got to spend an afternoon at the NASCAR race at Bristol Motor Speedway. And honestly? Talking sports is a great opportunity to connect with folks from all over the political spectrum about what’s going on in Washington. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106508372/541734216/1894416887?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Nascar_250425_T1_1_b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTgyNDUwZC1mYjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=JN322evRPfjOEgi3YiYj2V7pfy7-6bYC72uyXrVQlDE=) Whether it was catching up at the track or in town, I got to have open, honest conversations about the state of our country. And one thing came through loud and clear: **people are tired of the chaos.**

They’re tired of the Trump administration’s recklessness. This isn’t what he said he’d do for our country. And they told me that their friends and neighbors feel the same.

This isn’t anything new. What Virginians all across the Commonwealth want is leaders who will focus on delivering _real_ results for Americans – lowering costs, protecting our national security, and creating good-paying jobs. # [Thank the judges who are blocking Trump’s grab for power](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tebb179cc-7b12-4c80-a177-05730710148d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

---
| | | Trump has spent his first months in office issuing executive orders that attack our rights, dismantle important government programs, and stretch way beyond the authority of the presidency. And his MAGA allies in Congress continue to allow him to ignore our Constitution. Thankfully, Trump is facing pushback to his power grab in court, and there are a handful of judges who are keeping Trump in check. He's recently been handed a series of defeats in his efforts to block DEI initiatives, withhold funding from "sanctuary" jurisdictions, and add a proof-of-citizenship requirement to the federal voter registration form. As Trump faces more legal battles in the coming months, we hope more judges will enforce the Constitution and act as a much-needed check on Trump's quest for dictatorship. While some of my colleagues across the aisle have been closing off access to constituents and not holding Town Halls, I know that this is the time to lean in. That’s why since being sworn in on January 3rd, I’ve held 12 Town Halls — both online and in-person around the District.
We’ve brought on terrific co-hosts including both Senators, Congressman Hoyer, Congressman Raskin, Attorney General Brown, Labor Secretary Wu, County Executive Ball, and so many others!
This month alone, my team and I held these Town Halls in Severna Park, Elkridge, Annapolis, and Pasadena. These events have been an incredible opportunity not only to hear from you, but to connect you with my team on critical casework like Social Security benefits and IRS issues.
We’ve also sourced ideas from the community as to how we can better represent your interests. I’m taking everything that I’m hearing on the ground and bringing it back to Leader Jeffries in Washington to inform our strategy as Democrats going forward. I cannot tell you how inspiring and energizing it is to have so many folks continuing to show up and lean in at this moment — it’s what gives me hope even on our hardest days.
As your Representative I will always show up for you. Will you help by chipping into the fight? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q2-2025-em?refcode=blu_em_sefc_2025-04-25]

Trump sees it all crashing down around him. He's petrified
### The Projection is the Point: Trump Rails Against ActBlue While Drowning in Red (Ink and Flags)
Trump's attacking ActBlue for a few reasons. He sees his polling numbers, even if he denies it. He knows he's convinced many MAGA to see him like an outbreak of lice or rescinded tax refund. That this could crush his cretinous GOP brethren running in 2026, wiped out like a Trumper owning a farm. No, he doesn't care about them--much like Don Jr., **they 're not him!**--but he knows what Democrats with power will do.
On a related note, never far from surface--The Horror, The Horror--of his life. [He's an astonishingly weak, little baby](https://substack.com/redirect/ee1b754a-5e3a-4107-bd33-d22fd5194a60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the largest recorded victim complex on record. He's terrified of everything from germs to everyone laughing at him to losing. The latter is why he cheats at everything. Politics is part of everything.
Or, one can pretend a guy who took **tens of millions from small-dollar donors -- marking many as recurring donors without their knowledge--and used it to pay off lawyers, fund his golf cart parade and more**, is genuinely outraged(!) that [Democrats have a centralized platform](https://substack.com/redirect/ca9f934d-7e11-415f-8626-57af040138d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) where people give voluntarily and transparently.
Meanwhile, Trump and his party run what amounts to a **global money laundering operation** , with GOP campaigns [practically ](https://substack.com/redirect/2f40b239-ff55-4fcb-b019-dcf5a00c55ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[mainlining rubles](https://substack.com/redirect/2f40b239-ff55-4fcb-b019-dcf5a00c55ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and riyals**. From [Russian oligarchs funneling millions through shadowy PACs](https://substack.com/redirect/fe1ba5f7-f2ed-4a2e-8624-41f458f99226?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to Saudis who don't just buy hotels--[but purchase bone-saw silence](https://substack.com/redirect/446ca081-399e-428b-8dc9-aa53f58a1334?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and complicity--Trump's only complaint about foreign money is when it doesn't show up in his own bank account.
Yet, we still haven't gotten to one of the biggest reasons Trump's doing this, one our corporate media wont't talk about:[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/643b3e65-0e1f-4ce0-a437-1d35158fd115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[It's part of a longtime pattern of Republicans politicizing the government to attack sources of Democratic money and votes](https://substack.com/redirect/643b3e65-0e1f-4ce0-a437-1d35158fd115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for patently absurd reasons**. This has been going on for 30 years--as more and more of the GOP leadership's become rotten to the core.
**This didn 't start with Trump, it created him.**
They went after unions, because they helped fund Democrats. Trial lawyers? Targeted with "tort reform." ACORN? Dismantled over fake scandals. Planned Parenthood? Attacked with fake blood libel videos about "after birth abortion"--which exists in the same way Monsters Inc. does. Hell, [immigration's about this and they say it out loud](https://substack.com/redirect/cd548840-778f-4505-be86-31a23a95e435?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This is why when I had former right-wing GOP Congressman, Joe Walsh, on my weekly Substack show, "Amped Up w/ Cliff Schecter," Joe simply said, "I was an asshole. I was a jerk. **[People like me paved the way for Donald Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/a94c7dff-6107-41b1-b551-5283be2d001f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ...**" Walsh gets it was Tea Party madness, McConnell's destruction of the Senate and stolen Supreme Court Judges, etc., that primed the GOP base to become anti-democracy & pro-Trump.
**Leading Republicans, for over a quarter century, have acted like political termites --gnawing away at the very beams that hold up democracy**, one progressive support system at a time. Trump's just the loudest, dumbest mouthpiece yet--accusing others of playing dirty while swimming laps in a cesspool.

null – see that little girl in the photo? That’s me! Way before I had the honor of serving Michiganders in Congress and launching this battleground campaign to be Michigan’s next U.S. senator. I was about 12 or 13 years old there.
But don’t be fooled by school picture day (_and my trendy beaded necklace_). Growing up as the daughter of small-business owners – Mom and Dad had their own landscaping business – I was always around a lot of dirt, grease, grime, and heavy machinery. **I wouldn’t have had it any other way.**
My parents taught me the value of hard work – a value that binds all of us in Michigan together. After all, we’re the state that built America. The state that built the middle class.
In fact, do you know what one of my favorite memories is from growing up? When I got the keys to my first car, a used Oldsmobile Cutlass Supreme. That car represented the newfound freedom of teenage years. **But it was more to me than just that – it also meant I had a piece of Michigan. **
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106509640/541738621/-1649021094?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk72-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODA3NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYTNjMTdiNi1mZDIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC02MDQ1YmRlZDhjY2EiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPD_Xqi7fBIcxNNPGkml15JE3RnSpSSz-TmOk8HtUxI=)
I love Michigan. I love the people here. And I love that I’ve been able to fight for my state in Congress. But as I’ve traveled our state recently, it’s clear that the people I love are afraid. They’re afraid because of the chaos and uncertainty that Donald Trump and Elon Musk are inflicting upon our nation.
All across our state, I hear concerns about rising costs, fear of uncertainty in our auto industry, and worries about the future of Social Security and Medicare. And you better believe people are outright disturbed by Trump’s attacks on our democracy and personal freedoms. **This fear, uncertainty, and chaos – all of it is ****_unacceptable._**
That’s why I’m running for U.S. Senate. I’m ready to fight for the people I love and help block Trump’s dangerous agenda. But the path to the Senate majority runs right through Michigan – and this battleground race is already being called a “toss up” by elections experts.

That's right -- they just passed a bill lowering the recount threshold to 0.15 points. But they made this change across the board, right? To be fair? Of course not. Candidates for local elections and the state legislature can still request a recount if their race is within 1% (or 50 votes). For races for Congress and statewide office -- the most competitive races -- the tally must be within 0.15%. This is yet another case of opponents of voting rights changing the rules to protect themselves and their power. The law's vote manager claims that this bill was passed to "preserve fairness", while all it really does is protect his political party from potential losses while restricting campaigns from making sure every vote counts. If you've saved your payment information with FastAction, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | Those aren't the only changes -- this new law puts partisan county auditors and their staffs in charge of the recount instead of a board chosen by the campaigns in the race. Want to guess which party controls most of Iowa's county auditor positions? Yes, the one that just passed this bill into law.Take it from Iowa state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott, who has been through two recounts following elections for her Senate seat:"Currently in our process, the county auditor and their staff, they’re very present, they support the process, they’re very engaged ," she said. "But taking out the candidates’ representatives and the neutral party,putting it on a partisan elected official and the staff who are supervised and employed by them does not make it more fair. " It's clear that all this new law does is create opportunities for opponents of voting rights to suppress votes before they can be cast and the controlling party to silence votes after the election by having them tossed in a recount -- just like we're seeing in North Carolina with a race still not settled almost 6 months after Election Day. | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. Friend, Over 4 million Americans have shown up to multiple Hands Off Rallies in small towns to cities in all 50 states. This is what democracy looks like! I’ve had the opportunity to go to protests in my district and in Washington DC, and coming together with everyday people has given me hope that we can defeat fascism and the presidential administration’s cruel and lawless actions. We need more people getting involved right now, whether it’s in the streets or caring for our neighbors through mutual aid. Trump’s tariffs are already impacting ports and trucking, and could affect store shelves. Trump’s USDA has also cancelled crucial deliveries to food banks, with Michigan food banks losing $4.3 million worth of emergency food—about 2 million meals. **Our communities will be more in need with domino effects to come** as people have to start paying student loans again and we face cuts to food banks, school meals, and so many social safety net programs. * **Volunteer at and donate to local food banks.** (You can find many by entering your zip code on [Feeding America’s website.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMc1Co5pwXVguouYUfDKUKiq6tTOsQ3NhUlI4uqN2duKp4e49OMeUVP1_7GT4wklSHtHO0xNP4zyUWSl0AjK3zC1m8VyWEbcn72Dmf14SntPywCyksWu4-RvTz4Z0McbKD1S_fTQZeTvuutz4SP1w1vPyCO1ckMFSpAJe0Sqd21osFifgaIH8k4_32eta_E5B6q4c2N_XCGDhe-Kd5Y-wKro0yae81J48s8e8dOl9fhS0tW22znxZ-D8aUjkp9w1HKtscoP_578CeX7VfGqswQY30d0l5Z-6YMitxiJZIWLoY4J1flwD7TQZNhKKNhNjY1Q/4fy/dX99YJi9TYeTNig0vuB2Ow/h1/h001.qFDWXspV5rr3FuZaVwjdVCfNrHNQs4Hl9xre0SUazhk))
