name: Alea Nadeem
subject: Iraq stripped me of my freedom. America gave me a second chance.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alea for Congress
body:
Here’s my story
[ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=5a01dba9ac0f4575a5e3c07ab2ddc354&_e=8XGQPo6qp9kKM1EvBBwOQMMPFIvKLQ9tBb4_zWycpDch67pQbIoK3bQmLKGBe8PpIYLo3lxEBYTX9sKln4Lyd228Zjqc3fKgDkCWkdarg0wW614y15i0_Hdd1Ych9XxWavVlK0QeVtY7yPZdruzEWfJmP92bwo6AOg-WZZNJA_-H3qlfMJv_QP1RsJ8EQmXHH1AbIM_Ww72SpUKbxGoUl-c06rOTWu2BcZzxZK8HGoBOqaIElNoIb8kWTTWPLu4-HD0jWpnkXTGNhSsiW-eDf0rpoAmwRF7Mhk6ZAqrbdQsARHMXbg_m8gvrkiDMELC1DF78HObCKx8GxL75T5pz6bNwNcKzHOPEXPdumUTbfcz7dEXcyROE5WSeCD20lizGfVAjJWXpIROT8oe8SLQ5QQ%3D%3D)
Peter,
Hi! My name is Alea.
I was born in Toledo, Ohio to an American mother and an Iraqi father - I know - an unusual combination. When you are a kid, you don’t know where your parents are from, but you just know they are your parents. I was a normal kid, went to school, ate McDonalds, and spent weekends with my grandparents.
[ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=5a01dba9ac0f4575a5e3c07ab2ddc354&_e=8XGQPo6qp9kKM1EvBBwOQMMPFIvKLQ9tBb4_zWycpDch67pQbIoK3bQmLKGBe8PpIYLo3lxEBYTX9sKln4Lyd228Zjqc3fKgDkCWkdarg0wW614y15i0_Hdd1Ych9XxWavVlK0QeVtY7yPZdruzEWfJmP92bwo6AOg-WZZNJA_-H3qlfMJv_QP1RsJ8EQmXHH1AbIM_Ww72SpUKbxGoUl-c06rOTWu2BcZzxZK8HGoAObg4Ygr2HFu8SdeOKzA-nIqOgGHJoZxnHoADCaX-ehzs6_MhPvT5BuS2l5yb-FR_oW_-BCuLeZPslonZXd0Jc509nwiAokUL7tkbQB0IzKBiciAnspWaJfzsZ91BYXgzgP4EmcC0Ez3jcsBaFUG8xUR0cInDcmLpp9a79hs0hag%3D%3D)
At the age of eight, I was kidnapped to Iraq, unfortunately by my own father. My life has never been the same, but believe it or not, it made me who I am today.
**Being kidnapped and losing my freedom is what made me appreciate the freedoms so many in the U.S. take for granted. I know firsthand what it’s like to lose your freedom – and was forced to live under Saddam Hussein’s brutal and repressive regime in Iraq, where being a woman means having no rights, speaking out costs you your life, and your future is not your own.**
[ **_I want to tell you about myself and my story, and I hope that after reading this, you’ll consider supporting my campaign for Congress to defeat one of the most vulnerable Democrats in America and advance President Trump’s America First policies._** ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=5a01dba9ac0f4575a5e3c07ab2ddc354&_e=8XGQPo6qp9kKM1EvBBwOQMMPFIvKLQ9tBb4_zWycpDch67pQbIoK3bQmLKGBe8PpIYLo3lxEBYTX9sKln4Lyd228Zjqc3fKgDkCWkdarg0wW614y15i0_Hdd1Ych9XxWavVlK0QeVtY7yPZdruzEWfJmP92bwo6AOg-WZZNJA_-H3qlfMJv_QP1RsJ8EQmXHH1AbIM_Ww72SpUKbxGoUl-c06rOTWu2BcZzxZK8HGoBlJ27TDsegAuXKH8zg152D4mXdppEO9jW4irQvqtjzGsgvsfh_4c7LY83VrYfU0_MWGNLeWYpapKP5qO2gQmZiNRZ9xxvuLv9Y0IQuXrYI31i0OuoQZkbGKmDjNCzxpU1NZa4VHBqByl1zV6lNV4Y0nhEo10YgHK7FLbnuQ_HNWg%3D%3D)
When I was 8 and my sister was 3, we took a family trip with my parents to visit my father’s mother who was sick in Iraq. At first, it was a wonderful experience meeting family for the first time. **_But my entire world would soon change forever._**
The night before our flight back to America, my dad woke us up for a surprise trip to my aunt’s house for ice cream and candy. As any little kid would, we relished the excitement of being up past our bed time, playing after we had our fill of sweets. **But we soon realized both of our parents were nowhere to be found._That’s when my nightmare began._**
Hours that felt like months and several nights of crying myself to sleep passed before they returned. Our family members they left us with didn’t speak English and we didn’t speak Arabic.
When they finally did return, it wasn’t the happy reunion I hoped for. My father had given my mother a heartbreaking ultimatum: She could only take one of us back to America. Fearing for my sister who was only 3 years old, my mother made an impossible decision, and **I was left behind.**
As a young girl, I had no choice but to adjust to my new life.
I learned Arabic and went to school. My family helped me and tried to comfort me as much as possible. I was surrounded by good people in Mosul, _but I never stopped trying to get back to America–back to my home._
Following Operation Desert Storm, U.S. forces protected the civilian population in northern Iraq. I remember a U.S. helicopter landing near my home in Mosul. I desperately begged the aircrew to take me back home. Of course, they couldn’t, but I never lost sight of my goal – not once during my four years in Iraq.
**Neither did my mother.** I didn’t know this then, but she was working with the FBI and local government officials in Toledo to secure my return home. My father was arrested for kidnapping, and the court told him he could not be released until I was brought back to the United States.
Finally, **I was reunited with my mother and my life in Ohio.** I was 12 years old, and a lot changed since I was last in America. I spoke broken English and was behind academically. It was a tough road, but I made it slowly.
[ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=5a01dba9ac0f4575a5e3c07ab2ddc354&_e=8XGQPo6qp9kKM1EvBBwOQMMPFIvKLQ9tBb4_zWycpDch67pQbIoK3bQmLKGBe8PpIYLo3lxEBYTX9sKln4Lyd228Zjqc3fKgDkCWkdarg0wW614y15i0_Hdd1Ych9XxWavVlK0QeVtY7yPZdruzEWfJmP92bwo6AOg-WZZNJA_-H3qlfMJv_QP1RsJ8EQmXHH1AbIM_Ww72SpUKbxGoUl-c06rOTWu2BcZzxZK8HGoAuieOLeCLLBvghkNGNWfbEB9UcJcEIY5So43Mg2VD4tvcaT4BYUiIRLfaA17K_I0DIDR_NXpPQCZeqCTQro1puu-77hiAQ4s91r_bSuWyWuxTwTwt-X3j_x7u93c_ZiSEO5mK1cYcXLNnZIkYgLeYVO0pVF76fuDibV3LBu3rVJg%3D%3D)
As a junior in high school, I watched in horror as our country was attacked on September 11, 2001. I knew I had to do something – to lead by example and show my fellow Americans that, in fact, Arab Americans love our country – and to give back to the country that gave me a chance.
**So, I walked into an Air Force recruiting office and asked to do whatever job deployed the most.**
A year later, I was in basic training, learning to become an Airman.
[ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=5a01dba9ac0f4575a5e3c07ab2ddc354&_e=8XGQPo6qp9kKM1EvBBwOQMMPFIvKLQ9tBb4_zWycpDch67pQbIoK3bQmLKGBe8PpIYLo3lxEBYTX9sKln4Lyd228Zjqc3fKgDkCWkdarg0wW614y15i0_Hdd1Ych9XxWavVlK0QeVtY7yPZdruzEWfJmP92bwo6AOg-WZZNJA_-H3qlfMJv_QP1RsJ8EQmXHH1AbIM_Ww72SpUKbxGoUl-c06rOTWu2BcZzxZK8HGoAENh2mwVv-C-WIF2aiEMvwSJra4lp32XjCnihcd6vf4eP4HdprwnnPCkF7UBcNYe5aEVPATThHvsAXI7JARGvtTa-z6a3ct14k6zwQa4rFKXCYkY6FBd5wh2-meZAKVY-qKw7eHwOIkPhP_7TTFX3NRc0B4KaCnDRGGdFnaIF8Ig%3D%3D)
Since then, I’ve spent my career in military intelligence, serving both active duty and in the Air Force Reserve. Today I’m a Lieutenant Colonel. I’ve advised top military leaders, deployed to the Middle East, and used my experience to help America understand the culture and geopolitics of Iraq and Syria.

clean_body: Here’s my story Peter, Hi! My name is Alea. I was born in Toledo, Ohio to an American mother and an Iraqi father - I know - an unusual combination. When you are a kid, you don’t know where your parents are from, but you just know they are your parents. I was a normal kid, went to school, ate McDonalds, and spent weekends with my grandparents. At the age of eight, I was kidnapped to Iraq, unfortunately by my own father. My life has never been the same, but believe it or not, it made me who I am today. Being kidnapped and losing my freedom is what made me appreciate the freedoms so many in the U.S. take for granted. I know firsthand what it’s like to lose your freedom – and was forced to live under Saddam Hussein’s brutal and repressive regime in Iraq, where being a woman means having no rights, speaking out costs you your life, and your future is not your own. When I was 8 and my sister was 3, we took a family trip with my parents to visit my father’s mother who was sick in Iraq. At first, it was a wonderful experience meeting family for the first time. But my entire world would soon change forever. The night before our flight back to America, my dad woke us up for a surprise trip to my aunt’s house for ice cream and candy. As any little kid would, we relished the excitement of being up past our bed time, playing after we had our fill of sweets. But we soon realized both of our parents were nowhere to be found.That’s when my nightmare began. Hours that felt like months and several nights of crying myself to sleep passed before they returned. Our family members they left us with didn’t speak English and we didn’t speak Arabic. When they finally did return, it wasn’t the happy reunion I hoped for. My father had given my mother a heartbreaking ultimatum: She could only take one of us back to America. Fearing for my sister who was only 3 years old, my mother made an impossible decision, and I was left behind. As a young girl, I had no choice but to adjust to my new life. I learned Arabic and went to school. My family helped me and tried to comfort me as much as possible. I was surrounded by good people in Mosul, but I never stopped trying to get back to America–back to my home. Following Operation Desert Storm, U.S. forces protected the civilian population in northern Iraq. I remember a U.S. helicopter landing near my home in Mosul. I desperately begged the aircrew to take me back home. Of course, they couldn’t, but I never lost sight of my goal – not once during my four years in Iraq. Neither did my mother. I didn’t know this then, but she was working with the FBI and local government officials in Toledo to secure my return home. My father was arrested for kidnapping, and the court told him he could not be released until I was brought back to the United States. Finally, I was reunited with my mother and my life in Ohio. I was 12 years old, and a lot changed since I was last in America. I spoke broken English and was behind academically. It was a tough road, but I made it slowly. As a junior in high school, I watched in horror as our country was attacked on September 11, 2001. I knew I had to do something – to lead by example and show my fellow Americans that, in fact, Arab Americans love our country – and to give back to the country that gave me a chance. So, I walked into an Air Force recruiting office and asked to do whatever job deployed the most. A year later, I was in basic training, learning to become an Airman. Since then, I’ve spent my career in military intelligence, serving both active duty and in the Air Force Reserve. Today I’m a Lieutenant Colonel. I’ve advised top military leaders, deployed to the Middle East, and used my experience to help America understand the culture and geopolitics of Iraq and Syria. America gave me a second chance, and I am committed to continuing my service to this country with everything I have. My experiences have taught me that freedom isn’t free, and you never know what you had until you lose it. America needs strong leaders who understand that and who will stand up to ensure that future generations have a stronger, better, freer country than we inherited. Our military, our families, and our freedoms are worth fighting for. And I will never stop fighting for you and I will always put America First. I hope you will join me on this mission. Donald Trump just signed an executive order targeting ActBlue, the largest fundraising platform used by Democratic donors across the country.
| Fight for Progress is dedicated to building a more progressive America and has raised over half a million dollars for Democratic candidates. If you would like to donate to a deserving Democrat, you can do so _[here.](https://fight4progress.org/l/keicMO9GRvCZ)_ And of course, you can [_unsubscribe here_](https://fight4progress.org/l/KyztB6yHZzzf) at any time.

| Peter,

Donald Trump just signed an executive order targeting ActBlue, the largest fundraising platform used by Democratic donors across the country.

To be clear: this isn’t about election transparency. **This is about the Trump Administration abusing its power to brazenly attack American democracy.** Allegations that ActBlue funnels unlawful foreign contributions to campaigns in an attempt to influence elections are completely baseless.**ActBlue strictly adheres to the rule of law, whereas the Trump Administration abuses it for political gain.**

**We know why they’re doing this.** They understand the power of the grassroots momentum that we have on our side. They know that the tide is turning against them and that we are ready to win in 2025 and 2026\. This attack on ActBlue is a blatant weaponization of federal power by Donald Trump to silence all opposition.

**But we won’t be silenced.** _Donald Trump tried to subvert our elections once before, and failed, because Democrats didn’t back down._

[_**Fight For Progress is fighting to elect Democrats across the country in the 2025 and 2026 elections—because our democracy is worth fighting for—but we can’t do it alone. | | | Dear Friend, Your participation in Hillsdale College's **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** is requested.

Your response will only take a few minutes, but the subject is crucial to the future of liberty and the separation of powers in America.

The American Founders thought that the proper role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution.

But progressives see the Court differently. They want activist judges to legislate from the bench.
## Do you agree that the role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution as it is written and NOT to make laws or advance a particular policy agenda?
[YES](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/s/c/L-qkoQ67r-2LcLrvUGKeiOZj8ib6YjiuSHGA9zefyx9tiyzOUhUHHb6Ml2NeiXHm4pJ2fGi8y8PsdNur-ekV59NR9WpoSlbadJ-MjtAJclpB4rgopZnpyrnY1ZG_wICRDM1sV4F9zEEu7Y9BBczIj2hRar-lD3NhSPlgGMzCeCGFhoyQ9l0iPLujiCf-7JxRumZa9iBYo0DBG2NrmxXF59zh3wFF-Cj1lB-YfmDvpM0XIZ3iXWyLEkQYkpJk9cBia0XBeFT790NEt_PsbdRqOUzVR7esN8O7Ug6rYEk6ezx5HsVH2rOhmzB1ZXb-Wz_Evhg8GTTaNMxjHmzChW8SXci1vlOo-PGYZANlzQgWoED2w80R9dUKRBos1habtYl-SUyJQd55M9Rn7OVfI_uiOa-VC7wf-IXEnUJQUxSnfrQCmayDNImtIX0aLvqOZ9qsHQ/MRRrBaEyCuNqcxLcuhxLodmu9PGA_yZt/8) [NO](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/s/c/P5c9OIuBCnScFXJhRyi5RZDVwv3vVhMhGVk98QXNtJ-qeFMX4xv2gh2ttYLIkXoejuLgujPkU8X6EmZ46t2GuNGZo7x6vca9Z_WtjEVkNh4gF0HYrHtEqf1kX1XUMD18PSrvnN0kWCppWl4_zfNCK5Iu_LGo3se89aln3i2ZxABQWWpQPXK94vZRvpmCt_z6yGrYq3F4TXkE2SLWEK50o7hdLoFTtMstKWle26S2nHRy7Gr4Jx3ZbiTRoHJreS_n6wfdZyFaoROuaiBbo5l8VJGcIWJsJCTxWUgQ3QG5a1xpZJh6AZCXjQb4j-B7l8R2MV73g3tJVld5u70Nu-iYIehlNw7ww7WY9PnLXUljq40SeuFVE2soAui364u8E3mUCR9B-REdWUV-_aUHckvGkVvNSmyNGI2x12lw6mhHGizUbs0q60e5ztvMVB-YLfVzMQ/a-QuuuMidJFqW_neSyxjiZuZsMpb-cIq/8) Even worse, progressives dismayed by recent Supreme Court decisions want to "pack" the bench with additional justices to advance a preferred policy agenda.

As Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) put it in a _Boston Globe_ op-ed: "To restore balance and integrity to a broken institution, Congress must expand the Supreme Court by four or more seats."

That is why I'm reaching out to you today...

_What is your opinion about the Supreme Court 's role in our constitutional republic? _

Please share your thoughts with me using the College's **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** right away.

Your response will help Hillsdale form effective strategies to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty--including the proper role of an independent judiciary that applies the Constitution instead of legislating from the bench.

You can easily complete your **National Survey on the United States Supreme Court** using this secure link: **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/supreme-court-survey](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/s/c/dDIza03_p1k_d9pFsQIdYw6qY8hTWaQZh4mjagD-WmJcWNK21C5IWeAlMnT8pxDqXE4F8bAaDM53lzilNsGCs5bgVVSa8jbFqH_UU7hdVnVq6EMqGBfKZXLHJTQuizWjPrVNKN3AVunf4uifn87IGgdqKfPGH9Gf-bqQq6PC6Q0l4Rfp8Uo7VCFg20pfHNSm9LM2Gxm73XpzTpMU6pD0nGNVQuurUROPUSYnhlgaEogC7reBanEWquXXrzB9lUPxBgT11_H288yi2nysBdpf6zDaiTgHlKr__rt2Zqd21scA1XhTFq3tNNtIYV4KOdTxbvWdF2egWjIIjoL6AVfgkaGptO_-yKn-LtxX2trkYpYwl7YwZQDbRy3i6efwDZgHtfkZpE0Ljd0IiMViRFoDeh2XW70OOD23NwhBqCu0njJQY3VS_EcOXgWIfXZRMrzuHg/CTXqwO27IZtXwmQ-8t6nAZgZ2hTxvQUn/8)** Thank you for your time and attention--and for your support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn
President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing Truth - Defending Liberty since 1844

subject: Help me take back our libraries

| | For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros' Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you've noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating "the environment" to a type of religion. The "Teen Zone" is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here's what's really alarming. We can't just sit back and say, "Well, I'll just make sure my family doesn't go to "Drag Queen Story Hour" and we won't check out those inappropriate books." That may be good for your family – for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! **[**I hope you see why I need your help today.**](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svameb&__onlt=h)** My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980's family sitcom "Growing Pains" or from my work in inspirational movies like "Fireproof" and "Left Behind." I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what's far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So together with a small Christian book publisher aptly named **Brave Books** , I wrote "As You Grow" to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. And then we decided to go one step further and counter those awful "Drag Queen Story Hours" with a wholesome Story Hour of our own. Our idea was to read the classic books you and I grew up with plus new wholesome **Brave Books** that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn't like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected our request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep us out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that's original), **Brave Books** was accused of trying to "confuse and demoralize children," our supporters were described as "bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about," and on and on. I can't even print most things these radicals said because it's so vile. In the end we got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those Story Hours where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang "God Bless America," and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here's the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking **Brave Books** how they could host Story Hours of their own. And that's how our nationwide "See You at the Library Day" was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 360 libraries in 45 states. On the same day, we held hundreds of Story Hours to fill children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. **I went to as many "See You at the Library" events as I could in one day to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots...** ...for a very simple mission – to reject the Left's radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America's libraries. And this year, our ambitious goal is to expand "See You at the Library Day" to over 1,000 libraries reaching over 100,000 children. The exact date in August will soon be announced. And before then, what we need is you! It's going to be expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold Story Hours for 100+ children at each library – that's 100,000+ children in all. **[That's why I hope you'll give a sponsorship gift of $175, $350, $525 or more today.](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svameb&__onlt=h)** Your sponsorship gift will be used to send a "Story Hour Kit" to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who's organizing a "See You at the Library Day" event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for the little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. **Brave Books** is a small Christian company. They don't have the millions behind them like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our 1,000 Story Hours to counter the radical leftists who've taken control of our libraries. Knowing that, **[**please consider a sponsorship gift of $175.**](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svameb&__onlt=h)** That's enough to sponsor one entire "Story Hour Kit" yourself. Singlehandedly, you'll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. **[Whatever you can give whether it's $35, $175, or anything higher or lower please get your sponsorship gift in within the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we can get into this August!](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=svameb&__onlt=h)**

body:
It was never my intention to be a "traditional" representative, and that hasn't changed. Peter,

I want to take a minute to properly introduce myself. Not just the title or the resume, _but the person behind the ask._ Because if I’m showing up in your inbox asking for a bit of your hard-earned money, the least I can do is make sure you know who’s asking — _**and why it matters.**_

[**If you’re already familiar with who I am and why I’m fighting for St. Louis, go ahead and make a donation of $3, $5, or whatever feels right to you ahead of Wednesday’s crucial end-of-month fundraising deadline.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106522016/541780465/552493051?refcode=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=aee79870-1c22-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWVlNzk4NzAtMWMyMi1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VNC0Qr0-D2HNY0I6XqxNfXHHrZCFYjtVXihYq6DOhIc=)

When I was growing up in North County, I watched my family fight for fairness on the job. My grandfather led a historic strike at a steel mill in the 60s. I didn’t fully understand what it meant when I was a kid, but I remember the pride in his voice when he talked about it.

That strike wasn’t just about wages — it was about dignity and respect and the belief that hard work should mean a better life, not just barely scraping by. Now I’m in Congress, and I carry all of that with me. For me, this job isn’t about titles; it’s about impact and doing my best to leave the world a better place than what I was born into, just like my family did. That means digging deep into criminal justice reform and public safety, showing up for working families, protecting our environment, and investing in the public health systems that keep communities strong.

**My path to Congress wasn’t a traditional one.**

My experience comes from union halls and classrooms; courtrooms and council chambers. It comes from waiting tables, running phone lines for a telephone company, teaching at the same local community college I started taking classes at when I was 17, and bouncing between odd jobs to make ends meet — and I wouldn't trade any of it.

Every job I had, and every challenge I’ve faced, led me to where I am today. And in those moments when I was working double shifts at Shoney’s or grading papers as a professor at St. Louis Community College, I knew one day I would follow in the steps of my family and have a chance to fight for the same community that raised me.

But Peter, my experience also comes from knowing when to fight like hell and when to sit down and really listen. **I promise to keep showing up as myself...not just the guy in a suit on the House floor, but the kid in a proud union family, the biggest Cardinals and Mizzou fan, a barbecue purist (sorry, Kansas City), and someone who still knows his way around a community college classroom.**

We need a little more realness in politics. And right now, I'm going to be real with you: _My team and I need your help._

We’re coming up on a crucial fundraising deadline, and these benchmarks matter — not just because the political world is always watching, but because this work takes real resources. That’s the only way we build out our organizing, amplify our message, and stay ready for whatever’s next.

[**If you’re with me on this journey — whether you’ve been here since the beginning of my career in public service or since November — I hope you’ll consider chipping in $3 or anything you can before Wednesday’s end-of-month fundraising deadline >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106522018/541780469/552493051?refcode=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=aee79870-1c22-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWVlNzk4NzAtMWMyMi1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VNC0Qr0-D2HNY0I6XqxNfXHHrZCFYjtVXihYq6DOhIc=) clean_body: It was never my intention to be a "traditional" representative, and that hasn't changed. Peter, I want to take a minute to properly introduce myself. Not just the title or the resume, but the person behind the ask. Because if I’m showing up in your inbox asking for a bit of your hard-earned money, the least I can do is make sure you know who’s asking — and why it matters. = When I was growing up in North County, I watched my family fight for fairness on the job. My grandfather led a historic strike at a steel mill in the 60s. I didn’t fully understand what it meant when I was a kid, but I remember the pride in his voice when he talked about it. That strike wasn’t just about wages — it was about dignity and respect and the belief that hard work should mean a better life, not just barely scraping by. Now I’m in Congress, and I carry all of that with me. For me, this job isn’t about titles; it’s about impact and doing my best to leave the world a better place than what I was born into, just like my family did. That means digging deep into criminal justice reform and public safety, showing up for working families, protecting our environment, and investing in the public health systems that keep communities strong. My path to Congress wasn’t a traditional one. My experience comes from union halls and classrooms; courtrooms and council chambers. It comes from waiting tables, running phone lines for a telephone company, teaching at the same local community college I started taking classes at when I was 17, and bouncing between odd jobs to make ends meet — and I wouldn't trade any of it. Every job I had, and every challenge I’ve faced, led me to where I am today. And in those moments when I was working double shifts at Shoney’s or grading papers as a professor at St. Louis Community College, I knew one day I would follow in the steps of my family and have a chance to fight for the same community that raised me. But Peter, my experience also comes from knowing when to fight like hell and when to sit down and really listen. I promise to keep showing up as myself...not just the guy in a suit on the House floor, but the kid in a proud union family, the biggest Cardinals and Mizzou fan, a barbecue purist (sorry, Kansas City), and someone who still knows his way around a community college classroom. We need a little more realness in politics. And right now, I'm going to be real with you: My team and I need your help. We’re coming up on a crucial fundraising deadline, and these benchmarks matter — not just because the political world is always watching, but because this work takes real resources. That’s the only way we build out our organizing, amplify our message, and stay ready for whatever’s next. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- I'm so grateful to have you fighting alongside me. The conversations happening online with the various websites that report, discuss and analyze key moments in an election or candidate are the way of the future in the political world. With powerful algorithms and AI tools the folks over at Eyes Over are about 3 days ahead of traditional polling. This is crucial if a candidate needs to address a key point or issue at hand as the results come in real time. Well on today's show the CEO of Eyes Over, Christopher Wilson, is going to update us on their latest data. Instead of favorable or unfavorable, Eyes Over uses online sentiment and when it comes to folks like Senator Van Hollen, sentiment is abysmal. Van Hollen is at 32 percent after his recent trip to El Salvador. Even as the media hails him as some sort of champion, the truth is most people don't like or appreciate what he is doing. Online sentiment registers differently and the highest high is around 50 percent, well Karoline Leavitt right now is sitting at 45 percent, showing how adept she is in her high pressure role. Chris gives us crucial insight into Gubernatorial races in Virginia and New Jersey as well as the public's trust in institutions such as the military, church, Supreme court and Congress. AI aggregating tools and online conversations are the future of politics and Eyes Over is at the forefront.

name: Lisa Hoyos, LCV
subject: URGENT: Tell Lee Zeldin Not to Put Polluters First
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTI0Mjg5MDAS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjIwMDM3MjU0MwS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, This is urgent: 31 of the bedrock protections that keep our air and water safe are at risk,as EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin recently announced plans to roll back these
protections. Zeldin is trying to disregard the Clean Air Act and dismantle our ability to
clean up climate pollution that threatens our health and environment. His
Polluters First Agenda is a major giveaway for oil and gas CEOs who care more
about profits than stopping pollution. Zeldin’s Polluters First Agenda is putting lives at risk. Indeed, an estimated 200,000 liveswould have been saved by the 31 clean air and climate regulations he is
disbanding for the sole purpose of promoting fossil fuel industry profits. Write to EPA Administrator Zeldin and tell him not to put polluters first! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/- Under the Polluters First Agenda, people living in the U.S. will face more
illness, missed work days, and higher costs while polluting industries get a
free pass. Dismantling bedrock environmental protections will endanger millions
of lives by polluting our air and water, leading to more asthma attacks and
cancer, and more toxic chemicals poisoning our drinking water and our soil. Giving handouts to fossil fuel executives will harm us all and create higher
energy and health costs. Trump and Zeldin are again putting polluters over
people and fulfilling their promises to their Big Polluter allies.
Simultaneously, they are eroding the clean energy economy we have been working
to build. We need to make our voices heard. Tell EPA Administrator Zeldin: Please put the needs of the American people first by preserving EPA’s lifesaving protections and environmental standards. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/VXb6sXabLqc_ Thanks for being with us, Lisa Hoyos

name: The Democratic National Committee
subject: Update: Our largest-ever monthly investment into Democratic state and territory parties →
body:
---
Derek, **We need to elect Democrats who will act as a check against Trump and his disastrous policies.** And that work starts in our states. So we’re putting our money where our mouth is and making a historic investment in our state parties — take a look: **_BREAKING: DNC and ASDC Announce Largest-Ever Monthly Investment into Democratic State and Territory Parties_** The DNC recently announced a historic four-year agreement to deliver more resources into Democratic state and territory parties than ever before — delivering on Chair Ken Martin’s commitment to turbocharging investments in on-the-ground organizing and party building. Under the new State Partnership Program (SPP) agreement, each state party will receive a baseline of **$17,500 a month,** a $5,000 per month increase over the last agreement, and Republican-controlled states will receive an additional investment of $5,000 a month through the DNC’s Red State Fund, putting their total at **$22,500** every month. The combined investments total a monthly transfer of **more than $1 million** from the DNC to state parties — _the committee’s largest investment into Democratic state parties in history._ These resources will allow state parties to invest in critical infrastructure and staffing, strengthen their data and tech operations, build on-the-ground organizing programs, and better prepare for upcoming election cycles — not just in the months ahead but in the years to come. Additionally, the new agreement includes the DNC’s commitment to hosting six regional training “bootcamps” for state parties per two-year cycle and the hiring of new ASDC staff, including five regional directors. **State parties are the backbone of the Democratic Party, and through this investment, our state parties will receive the support they need to show voters that no matter where they live, there is a strong Democratic Party in their corner, protecting their rights and working to check Trump’s power.** [These investments are only possible with your help. If initiatives like these are important to you, we hope you’ll consider pitching in a few dollars to help fund the work we’re doing:](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2025?refcode=em_20250425_3268_fr&amount=3&refcode2=3288_22930333_6FdZeu&akid=3288%2E22930333%2E6FdZeu) **[CONTRIBUTE $3](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2025?refcode=em_20250425_3268_fr&amount=3&refcode2=3288_22930333_6FdZeu&akid=3288%2E22930333%2E6FdZeu)** Thank you, and we’ll have more updates to share soon. name: Deb Haaland
subject: I am 35 years sober
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
You must face hard truths if you want to make change.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=1559%2E400544%2EDLhM_e)
I want to tell you about a milestone I’m proud of: **I have reached 35 years of sobriety.**
Most people running for office wouldn’t choose to speak candidly about alcohol addiction. But I’m not like most people running for office. My story is different.
I was about 23 years old when I made the brave decision to get sober. It was a struggle at first, but I persevered because I was committed to doing all I could. I went to AA meetings and probably read 20 books on addiction.
My struggles made me fierce, which is why I chose to speak openly about my sobriety in my very first campaign ad when I ran for Congress, which aired 7 years ago this week. And I’m so glad I did. I'll never forget the day we went to the Marigold Parade in the South Valley, and people came up to me right and left and thanked me for saying that in my ad. They shared stories about themselves, their parents, and their loved ones struggling with addiction, and it brought tears to my eyes that people felt represented by someone like me.
**My journey to sobriety taught me that you must face hard truths if you want to make change, which is why I’ll never shy away from the tough fights that lie ahead for New Mexico.**
Crime, poverty, homelessness, and addiction are weighing heavy on our state, and I intend to tackle those challenges head-on as governor. I promise to be honest about topics other politicians might try to sweep under the rug, because I believe if we’re brave, we can heal.
Thank you for hearing my story. That’s how we’ll win this race — by sharing our stories, lifting each other up, and being fierce enough to fight for the bright future New Mexicans deserve. **[If you can, I’d be grateful if you’d pitch in $5 so we can keep traveling New Mexico to hear from voters and win this race.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250425_1_sobriety?amount=5&refcode=em20250425-1559&refcode2=1559_400544_DLhM_e&akid=1559%2E400544%2EDLhM_e)**

Thank you for everything,
Deb
